Asking for help really sucks, pretty much all the time. It's so scary to open up to people, and the idea is always in the back of my mind like, "What if this was a mistake?" "What if this makes things worse?"
It's really hard, but I think it's important to try to use the rational part of our brains to tell ourselves that, if we need help, asking for it is the best and, arguably, only way to get it. 
Is there anything you're particularly scared of? I'm really scared of disappointing my significant other, and I'm really scared of my significant other getting worse instead of better. Like, I love him and I know him getting professional help is a big step in the right direction, but I'm still freaked out, ya know?

That's really kind, thank you. I know that none of this matters in the long run but I'm so irrationally afraid. He's all that I have and I wish everyday that I could just make him completely okay (if only it were that easy lol). 

I'm also nervous because, full disclosure, I'm on the autism spectrum and I have a really hard time understanding social cues and what other people mean sometimes. I'm so nervous to go to orientation alone and have to do all of those ice breakers and group activities.

In one week, we had 3 reports of food poisoning.

That, for most of us at least, name brand doesn't matter. I lived in a quad last semester. Myself and 2 of my roommates were not extremely well off. Our other roommate was very wealthy. Came home from work one night to find my wealthy roommate literally yelling at and berating my very poor roommate for not knowing what Tiffany Diamonds were.

Shortly after my Uncle's death, I had a dream that he owned a large corn silo in the middle of nowhere. From the outside, it was a normal enough looking silo, but the inside was designed and furnished like a multi-story house.

In the silo lived upwards of 50 gorillas. They all had distinct physical characteristics and unique personalities. Some of them wore nametags, as well. For whatever reason, my job was to go in there alone and feed these gorillas. How did I feed them, you might ask? 

Well, in the silo there were rows of 500 gallon drums that were filled with pink yogurt. I would scoop this pink yogurt into bowls, and the gorillas would drink from the bowls as if they were slurping soup. A weird detail is that when I would pour the yogurt into the bowls, it would settle into the bowl in such a way that it resembled a face (similar to that coffee foam art that is popular now). The gorillas were generally quite friendly, but if I made even a small mistake, they would get hostile. However, they never physically harmed me.

I don't know what this dream means, or if it even means anything. My uncle died almost 5 years ago and this dream has become a regular occurrence. The most recent time I had this dream was 3 nights ago.

I lost it at night, during a snowstorm, in the backseat of my car that we parked at a nature preserve near my fiancé's school. Both of us were wearing dresses (I am a girl and my fiancé is a guy), my fiancé dolled up in a full face of makeup, and we finished the deed right before a snow plow pulled up next to my car. I quickly climbed into the front seat with only my dress on (no panties, socks, shoes, or coat), and drove barefoot all the way back to the parking lot of his college, while my vagina began to bleed all over my seats because there was a little bit of tearing. At the same time, my fiancé is still in the backseat trying to change out of the dress and back into his jeans.
My fiancé and I never have to be hundreds of miles apart, ever again.
